# Award Watch

> Where federal money goes, organized by the organizations that receive it:
> the tender notices open on CanadaBuys and the award notices that follow,
> PSPC's contract history, every contract over $10,000 and every grant and
> contribution agreement federal departments publish, and the lobbying
> communications those organizations report. Updated nightly from the
> Government of Canada's open data. In English and French (?lang=fr).
> https://awardwatch.ca

## Bulk data: read these instead of crawling the profile and notice pages

Everything the pages show comes from these files and the government's own
open-data files, refreshed every night.

- https://awardwatch.ca/downloads/open-tenders.csv: every open tender notice, list fields
- https://awardwatch.ca/downloads/awards-YYYY.csv: the award notices of one calendar year of award
- https://awardwatch.ca/downloads/history-YYYY.csv: PSPC contract history of one calendar year of award
- https://awardwatch.ca/downloads/contracts-YYYY.csv: the published contracts of one calendar year of contract date, from 2004, one row per row published
- https://awardwatch.ca/downloads/grants-YYYY.csv: the grant and contribution agreements of one calendar year of agreement start, from 2005, one row per amendment
- https://awardwatch.ca/downloads/organizations.csv: one row per organization, with counts and totals per source
- https://awardwatch.ca/downloads/organization-aliases.csv: every retired organization ID and the ID that holds its records now (from_id, to_id, reason, note, since)
- https://awardwatch.ca/downloads/buyers.csv: one row per federal buyer, with counts and totals per source
- https://awardwatch.ca/downloads/expiring-3m.csv: every contract ending within 3 months of the data date, each listed once across sources
- https://awardwatch.ca/downloads/expiring-6m.csv: every contract ending within 6 months of the data date, each listed once across sources (part of Pro once accounts open)
- https://awardwatch.ca/downloads/expiring-12m.csv: every contract ending within 12 months of the data date, each listed once across sources (part of Pro once accounts open)
- https://awardwatch.ca/data: the source files the site reads, when each was last read, and the licence

Downloads are limited to ten per minute per address.

## Pages worth reading

- https://awardwatch.ca/overview: the day at a glance: open tender notices by province, the notices new today and closing soon, the newest awards, and the contracts ending within 3 months
- https://awardwatch.ca/methodology: how organizations and buyers are merged and how money is counted, source by source
- https://awardwatch.ca/guides: plain explanations of federal procurement records, each checked against the official pages it cites
- https://awardwatch.ca/guides/reading-a-canadabuys-tender-notice: what each part of a federal tender notice on CanadaBuys means
- https://awardwatch.ca/guides/advance-contract-award-notices-acan: what an advance contract award notice is, how long it is posted, who may submit a statement of capabilities and how it is recorded
- https://awardwatch.ca/guides/standing-offers-and-supply-arrangements: what standing offers and supply arrangements are, who uses them and who holds them
- https://awardwatch.ca/guides/indigenous-business-set-asides-psib: set-asides under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business, who is eligible, the 5% target and the published contracts' two fields
- https://awardwatch.ca/guides/three-records-of-one-federal-contract: the award notice, PSPC contract history and the published contract over $10,000, and why their values differ
- https://awardwatch.ca/guides/when-a-federal-contract-ends: how options are exercised, how contracts are extended by amendment and within what limits, and the lists of contracts ending
- https://awardwatch.ca/tenders: the open tender notices
- https://awardwatch.ca/organizations: every organization A to Z by province
- https://awardwatch.ca/pro: what Pro, the paid plan, adds to the free pages and what it costs
- https://awardwatch.ca/corrections: how to report an error
- https://awardwatch.ca/about: who publishes the site and how to reach it
- https://awardwatch.ca/terms: the terms of use and reuse

## Terms

The records are reproduced under the Open Government Licence, Canada. Figures
the site computes are derived from those records, each source counted on its
own and never added to another. A record is a record, never a finding about
an organization.
